newsitem.title: UK: More spread mileage ahead for Italian Government Bonds.
newsitem.headline: More spread mileage ahead for Italian Government Bonds.

text.p: With one last corner to negotiate before the lira can return to Europe's exchange rate grid, Italian government bonds (BTPs) are revving up for another burst of strong outperformance, analysts said on Monday.

While some see a period of consolidation for the 10-year BTP/German government bond spread after its spirited push down to the current 195 basis point level, others say investors should gear up for a move to 150 basis points in the near term.
"It is ERM high noon for the lira," said David Brown, chief international economist at Bear Stearns in London.
"The one last hurdle is the passage of the 1997 budget."

Italy's lower house, the Chamber of Deputies, has until November 14 to ratify the government's 1997 budget, which aims to slash 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) off the deficit in a dash to make it to the starting line for Europe's planned single currency.
The ERM (Exchange Rate Mechanism) sets currency fluctuation bands for member currencies. Grid membership is a precondition for monetary union, as laid down in the Maastricht Treaty.
Some political analysts say Prime Minister Romano Prodi may have to use confidence votes to squeeze the bill through.
While Brown said some last-minute nerves for BTP investors may come if confidence votes are called into play, he said this would serve only as a buying opportunity before a rally.

"Then we get the dust covers off for Italian convergence trades," Brown said. "The lira will go through the roof, interest rates will crash very sharply, the BTP curve will steepen aggressively and we will race in to 150 basis points on the BTP/Bund 10-year spread."

Italy's treasury and finance ministers both indicated in the past week that the lira could make the ERM move this month, but Prime Minister Prodi said last Friday that no date was yet set, although it was likely to come before the end of the year.

Like Brown, other analysts noted the prospect of a budget ratification this week, and favourable inflation data and possible ERM re-entry before the end of the November, but said after recent outperformance of 10-year BTPs over Bunds, the market had priced in much of the potential bond-positive news.
Andrew Bevan, senior bond economist at Goldman Sachs in London, said the 10-year yield spread offered little excitement, but suggested looking elsewhere in Italy for value.

"We feel more confident about the front end of the yield curve," he said. "The market is discounting quite an aggressive cut in short-term interest rates, but we think the central bank may move a bit earlier than the market is anticipating."

Bevan advised going for the three-year Italian paper and suggested establishing long positions in the short end of the futures market. "We would be outright long of the Eurolira contracts, particularly March Eurolire, and would prefer to be at the front end of the cash yield curve."
March Eurolire is trading at 93.28, pricing in three-month lira rates of 6.72 percent at expiry compared with 7.47 percent now. The Italian discount rate is currently 7.5 percent.

Luca Jellinek, bond strategist at Paribas Capital Markets, said the passing of the budget on Thursday may offer spread investors "a few basis points" of outperformance. He expected a correction once the 10-year gap reached 185 basis points.

"But in general our outlook is for spread convergence to continue in the longer-term," he said. Analysts said there was some potential for "external events" to put 10-year BTP holders at risk, adding weight to the argument for shuffling down the curve and setting up a defence.
"We are a bit nervous about one or two things from a global perspective which could prove to to be a threat," said Bevan. ($1=1521 Lire)
